text:
maria: Heads up — our Windows GitHub Actions runners started getting intermittent 401s against the Redwood API. Linux runners work fine. Anyone seen a platform-specific Basic auth quirk?
jamal: Do you mean you're sending an Authorization: Basic header yourself, or are you using the SDK which sets auth for you?
maria: We're constructing the Basic header in PowerShell in a workflow step because the app is a tiny script that uses curl. Example from the job (simplified):
```
- name: set env
  run: echo "REDWOOD_KEY=${{ secrets.REDWOOD_KEY }}" >> $GITHUB_ENV

- name: call api (pwsh)
  shell: pwsh
  run: |
    $k = $env:REDWOOD_KEY
    $b = [Convert]::ToBase64String([Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetBytes("$k:"))
    curl -H "Authorization: Basic $b" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
```
olga: Two common failure modes: trailing newline/CR in the secret (from how it's written to GITHUB_ENV) or accidental double-encoding if you use an SDK that already glues the header.
sam: On Windows pwsh, Get-Content and some ways of writing to $GITHUB_ENV can leave a trailing `\r` or `\n`. That changes the base64 payload so the server sees a different key -> 401.
jamal: Try trimming before encoding: `$k = $env:REDWOOD_KEY.Trim()` in pwsh. Or in bash use `printf '%s' "$SECRET" >` or `tr -d '\r'` when reading.
ci-bot: Note: GH runner `echo 'FOO=bar' >> $GITHUB_ENV` always appends a newline — that's expected. Problem is when the consumer code keeps the newline in the value when building the header on Windows (CRLF becomes part of the string).
maria: Tried `.Trim()` — that fixed the 401s on the Windows runners, thanks. One follow-up: is it better to use `Authorization: Bearer` or `X-API-Key`? Curious about SDL or proxies that rewrite Basic.
jamal: Redwood accepts API keys in either `Authorization: Basic <base64(api_key:)>` or `Authorization: Bearer <key>` and `x-api-key` as a fallback for some infra. Best practice: let your HTTP client send a raw apiKey in an SDK config if available. SDKs typically expect the plain key and set header correctly — don't pre-base64 if you're passing into an SDK.
devex-bot: FYI — our Node SDK will set `Authorization` if you call `new RedwoodClient({ apiKey: '...' })`. If you also add an Authorization header manually (pre-encoded) you may end up with conflicting headers.
olga: Another wrinkle — when the key contains non-ASCII (rare, but happens with some rotated keys), `btoa` in browsers uses latin1 and will break. Use UTF-8 encoding before base64 (Buffer in Node or [Text.Encoding] in pwsh) — which you already do in pwsh example.
sam: Quick checklist if you see Windows-only 401s:
• Check how the secret is written to GITHUB_ENV (use `printf`/`echo` consistently).
• Trim `\r` and `\n` in pwsh: `$env:REDWOOD_KEY = $env:REDWOOD_KEY.Trim()`.
• If using SDKs, pass raw key to SDK instead of pre-building Authorization header.
• Avoid double-encoding: don't call Buffer.from(...).toString('base64') if SDK already encodes.
maria: Great — applied Trim and switched to passing key to the SDK in our small service path. All green. Thanks :rocket:
jamal: Nice. If anyone hits this in CI, ping me and I can add a tiny GH Actions snippet to the devex quickstart.
ci-bot: Deploy bot: canary tests that were failing have now passed on the latest run. :white_check_mark:
